concept_summary: Honey Cove Restaurant: a 120-seat, 3,953 sq ft full-service restaurant with commercial kitchen, no alcohol, operating on the first story and mezzanine (second story) at 2573 Mission St in the Mission Street NCT zoning district.

overall.line: Of the 3 approvals this concept needs: 3 not permitted (zoning and use, health permit, building permit and change of use).
overall.next_step: Request a written zoning determination from San Francisco Planning Department confirming whether the mezzanine is counted as a second story under Section 754 and whether the district's 179 eating-and-drinking-use cap has been reached; do not file a CUA application or pay fees until both answers are…

lines.text: The concept is looked up as a Restaurant (Planning Code § 102).
Zoning district NCT-MISSION: a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 754, in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)).

The concept is not described as serving alcohol, so the liquor licence rules of Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District were not applied.

approvals.summary: Planning Code Section 754 prohibits restaurants on the second story in NCT-MISSION and caps total eating-and-drinking uses at 179; the records do not show the current use count against the cap.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 754 Table (in force from January 14, 2024) lists a Restaurant on the first story in NCT-MISSION as a conditional use, but a Restaurant on the second story as not permitted.
findings.verification_note: The record shows restaurant_permission as 'unknown' and does not provide the story-by-story permissions or the effective date.

findings.text: The same table caps eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) in the district at 179 total (Table 754 Note 7); a new one is not permitted if it would exceed that cap, and the records do not show how many uses currently exist.
findings.verification_note: The record references Table 754 but does not state the cap of 179 or the rule about exceeding the cap.

findings.text: The concept occupies both the first story and a mezzanine (described as second story in the profile assumptions); whether a mezzanine is counted as a second story under Section 754 depends on its size, openness and Building Code classification, which only plans or an inspection can establish.

Two prior CUA applications at the adjacent 2575 Mission St (same parcel) for restaurants with Type 47 licenses were withdrawn (2021-005782CUA, filed June 2021, withdrawn August 2024) and cancelled (2018-016814CUA, filed December 2018, cancelled June 2021).
findings.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

findings.text: One comparable restaurant CUA at 3224 22nd St (108 m away, NCT-MISSION) was approved September 2023 for a change from limited to full restaurant; that project was single-story with Type 41 beer-and-wine license, and the Commission approved it 7-0 after three months with standard sidewalk-maintenance, soundproofing, odor-control and community-liaison conditions.
findings.verification_note: The record does not state that the project was single-story.

findings.text: A September 2024 agency referral noted that the NCT-MISSION district had 167 eating and drinking uses, below the 179 cap; the records do not show whether the count has since increased or whether merging two storefronts at 2573 and 2575 Mission would count as one or two uses.
findings.verification_note: The record does not mention a 179 cap.

basis.text: Zoning does not permit a new Restaurant at this address, and no City department may issue a permit or licence that would authorize a use the Planning Code prohibits: not permitted.

approvals.summary: The cited records did not support this summary. See the findings below.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 175(a) states that no department may issue a permit or licence that would authorize a use the Planning Code prohibits at that location.
findings.verification_note: The cited zoning district record does not contain or reference Planning Code Section 175(a) or its provisions about permit issuance.

findings.text: DPH health permit applications for limited restaurants in NCT-MISSION are routinely approved within 1–4 weeks as agency referrals when the use is principally permitted under Section 754; the adjacent 2567 Mission St received DPH approval in eight days (2020-001243MIS, filed January 28, 2020, approved February 5, 2020).
findings.verification_note: The record shows one case taking 8 days but does not state applications are routinely approved within 1–4 weeks. The record shows 11m distance but does not state the location is adjacent.

findings.text: A full-service restaurant with 120 seats and commercial kitchen will require DPH plan check ($2,207 for new restaurant, eight hours review) and a pre-opening inspection with a certified food safety manager on staff before the health permit is issued.
findings.verification_note: The records state the fee and requirements but do not establish that this specific restaurant scenario will require plan check.

conditions: Additional Project Authorization: The Project Sponsor shall obtain operating licenses from Alcoholic Beverage Control prior to commencing any Liquor Sales, wine tastings or other activities per Planning Code Section 202.2(a)(1) and Planning Code Interpretations. Monitoring - After Entitlement

Validity: The authorization and right vested by virtue of this action is valid for three (3) years from the effective date of the Motion. The Department of Building Inspection shall have issued a Building Permit or Site Permit to construct the project and/or commence the approved use within this three-year period. (standard)

Expiration and Renewal: Should a Building or Site Permit be sought after the three (3) year period has lapsed, the project sponsor must seek a renewal of this Authorization by filing an application for an amendment to the original Authorization or a new application for Authorization. Should the project sponsor decline to so file, and decline to withdraw the permit application, the Commission shall conduct a public hearing in order to consider the revocation of the Authorization. (standard)

Diligent Pursuit: Once a site or Building Permit has been issued, construction must commence within the timeframe required by the Department of Building Inspection and be continued diligently to completion. Failure to do so shall be grounds for the Commission to consider revoking the approval if more than three (3) years have passed since this Authorization was approved. (standard)

Extension: All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay. (standard)

Conformity with Current Law: No application for Building Permit, Site Permit, or other entitlement shall be approved unless it complies with all applicable provisions of City Codes in effect at the time of such approval. (standard)

Enforcement: Violation of any of the Planning Department conditions of approval contained in this Motion or of any other provisions of Planning Code applicable to this Project shall be subject to the enforcement procedures and administrative penalties set forth under Planning C ode Section 176 or Section 176.1. The Planning Department may also refer the violation complaints to other city departments and agencies for appropriate enforcement action under their jurisdiction. (standard)

Revocation due to Violation of Conditions: Should implementation of this Project result in complaints from interested property owners, residents, or commercial lessees which are not resolved by the Project Sponsor and found to be in violation of the Planning Code and/or the specific conditions of approval for the Project as set forth in Exhibit A of this Motion, the Zoning Administrator shall refer such complaints to the Commission, after which it may hold a public hearing on the matter to consider revocation of this authorization. Operation (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (A): The business operator shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. In addition, the operator shall be responsible for daily monitoring of the sidewalk within a one-block radius of the subject business to maintain the sidewalk free of paper or other litter associated with the business during business hours, in accordance with Articl e 1, Section 34 of the San Francisco Police Code. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (B): When located within an enclosed space, the premises shall be adequately soundproofed or insulated for noise and operated so that incidental noise shall not be audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels specified in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (C): While it is inevitable that some low level of odor may be detectable to nearby residents and passersby, appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed in conformance with the approved plans and maintained to prevent any significant noxious or offens ive odors from escaping the premises. (standard)

Eating and Drinking Uses (D): Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company. Trash shall be contained and disposed of pursuant to garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines set forth by the Department of Public Works. (standard)

Sidewalk Maintenance: The Project Sponsor shall maintain the main entrance to the building and all sidewalks abutting the subject property in a clean and sanitary condition in compliance with the Department of Public Works Streets and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards. (standard)

Community Liaison: Prior to issuance of the Alcoholic Beverage License type 41 by the State of California, the Project Sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with the issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties. The Project Sponsor shall provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups for the area with written notice of the name, business address, and telephone number of the community liaison. Should the contact information change, the Zoning Administrator and registered neighborhood groups shall be made aware of such change. (standard)
comparable_cases.why_comparable: Nearest approved restaurant CUA (108 m, 3224 22nd St), same NCT-MISSION zoning, same change-of-use scenario (limited to full restaurant with Type 41 beer-and-wine license). Decided September 2023 with 7-0 approval after a three-month process. This is a use decision.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a full restaurant upgrade just one block away, showing that restaurant CUAs in NCT-MISSION can succeed when the concept is straightforward (no second-story restaurant issue, no Type 47, no mezzanine merger). Standard conditions: sidewalk maintenance, soundproofing, odor control, trash management, community liaison. The three-month timeline (filed June, decided September) i…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Very close (91 m, 2534 Mission St), same NCT-MISSION zoning, restaurant expansion (Foreign Cinema adding adjacent vacant space). Cancelled October 2024 after more than eight years. This is a use decision.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Even an established, well-regarded restaurant (Foreign Cinema) abandoned its expansion CUA after eight years in the pipeline, indicating that expansion or merger projects on this corridor face extended timelines and uncertain outcomes. The fact that it was not denied but cancelled suggests the sponsor lost patience or financing; operators should budget for multi-year CUA processes.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Same adjacent property (11 m, 2567 Mission St), same NCT-MISSION zoning. DPH referral for a limited restaurant, approved February 2020 as a permitted use under Section 754. This is an agency referral, not a Commission hearing.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referrals for limited restaurants (no alcohol, daytime hours, limited prep) are approved quickly and routinely on this block; the problem arises when a project proposes full-service dining, alcohol, second-story occupancy, or storefront mergers that trigger conditional-use review. Honey Cove's 120-seat, two-story, merged-storefront profile will require a CUA, not a simple referral.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Very close (87 m, 2526–2548 Mission St), same NCT-MISSION zoning. CUA approved December 1993 for expansion of a fast-food taqueria in the Mission Restaurant Use Sub-District under old code sections 781.5 and 186.1(b). This is a use decision.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A restaurant expansion CUA was approved in 1993 on the same block, but under the old NC-3 and Mission RU Sub-District rules; the district has since been rezoned to NCT-MISSION with new conditional-use triggers (Section 754) and the Mission Alcohol SUD overlay. Conditions and timelines from 30+ years ago offer little guidance for today's process, but the approval shows the corridor has long hosted…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Nearby (164 m, 3218 21st St), same NCT-MISSION zoning. DPH referral for a new limited restaurant (Signy's Pizza), approved September 2024 as a principally permitted use under Section 754; the referral noted that total eating and drinking uses do not exceed 167 within the Mission Street NCT. This is an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: As of September 2024 the NCT-MISSION district had not yet reached the 179 eating-and-drinking-use cap imposed by Planning Code Section 754 Table Note 7; a new restaurant was approved as permitted because the total was only 167. Honey Cove needs to confirm the current count before filing, as the records do not show whether the cap has since been reached.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Very close (127 m, 3233 22nd St), same NCT-MISSION zoning. DPH referral for a restaurant, approved March 2024 within 11 days. This is an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Simple DPH referrals for restaurants that are principally permitted (first-story, no alcohol complications, no use-size trigger) are approved in under two weeks. Honey Cove's second-story mezzanine and 3,953 sq ft will trigger a CUA, not a fast-track referral.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Very close (109 m, 2512 Mission St), same NCT-MISSION zoning. DPH referral for a restaurant, approved May 2021 within one month. This is an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Routine restaurant agency referrals are approved within 1–4 weeks when the use is permitted by right under Section 754; the CUA path (required for Honey Cove due to second-story dining under Section 754) adds 4–8 months for Commission hearings, neighborhood notification, and discretionary review risk.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Very close (108 m, 3242 22nd St), same NCT-MISSION zoning. DPH referral for a limited restaurant, approved October 2020 within five weeks. This is an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Limited restaurants (no full bar, minimal prep, smaller footprints) are approved as agency referrals within weeks; Honey Cove's 120-seat, full-kitchen, two-story profile will require a discretionary CUA hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Very close (109 m, 2512 Mission St), same NCT-MISSION zoning. ABC referral for a Type 41 beer-and-wine restaurant with nighttime entertainment (dba Arcana), approved November 2020 within three weeks. This is an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Even a restaurant with a Type 41 license and entertainment was approved as an agency referral (not a CUA) because it was principally permitted under Section 754 and the nighttime entertainment was accessory. Honey Cove avoids alcohol, which simplifies the path, but the second-story restaurant use under Section 754 will still trigger a CUA.

filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning Department Current Planning Division to confirm the mezzanine classification and the district use count.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Bring a floor plan showing the mezzanine square footage, openness to the first story, and proposed occupant load. Ask: (1) Is the mezzanine counted as a second story under Section 754, and if so is there any path to a variance or exception for mezzanine dining when first-story dining is conditional use? (2) What is the current count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION against the 179 cap in Table 754 Note 7, and does merging two storefronts count as one or two uses? Request written confirmation of both answers before filing any application or paying any fees.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms in writing that the mezzanine is not a second story and the district use count is below 179, proceed with entity formation, business registration and a fictitious business name filing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization with the California Secretary of State ($70), obtain a federal EIN from the IRS (free, same day online), register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector (Business Registration Certificate, $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts, 1–5 days), and file a fictitious business name statement with the SF County Clerk if the public name differs from the LLC name ($60–$120, then publish once a week for four weeks and file proof within 45 days).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Before opening, register for state and local taxes, obtain workers' compensation insurance, enroll employees in food handler training, and secure ASCAP and BMI licenses for recorded music.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File for a California Seller's Permit with CDTFA (free, 1–14 days online) and register as an employer with EDD if you have employees (free, 1–7 days, needs the EIN). Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (mandatory from the first employee; premiums are 2–6% of payroll for restaurant class codes). Each employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire ($7–$15, online, one day). Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music ($300–$2,500 per year each, formula-based on occupancy and music use, 1–7 days online). Set up organics (green bin) collection with the City hauler per SB 1383.

timeline_cost.notes: No timeline or cost is given because zoning does not permit a restaurant on the second story at this address under Planning Code Section 754, and the records do not establish whether the mezzanine is counted as a second story or whether the district's 179 eating-and-drinking-use cap has been reached. The operator must obtain written confirmation from San Francisco Planning Department that (1) the mezzanine is not a second story under Section 754, and (2) the current use count in NCT-MISSION is below the 179 cap, before any application is filed or any fees are paid. If Planning confirms both in writing, the pathway is a Conditional Use Authorization (4–8 months, $3,100–$15,000 CUA fee) plus building permit with DPH plan check (2–4 months in parallel, $800–$15,000 building permit fee + $2,207 DPH plan check), health permit ($470), business registration ($55–$700), entity formation ($70), and state/local setup costs ($0–$500), for a total of approximately 6–12 months and $5,000–$35,000 in government fees and professional services to opening day, excluding construction costs. If Planning states the mezzanine is a second story or the use cap has been reached, there is no approval path and no cost or time estimate applies.

records_summary: The records show 2573 Mission St (parcel 3615/020) sits in the Mission Street NCT zoning district and the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. The pathway analysis indicates that a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use, but a Restaurant on the second story is not permitted under current Planning Code Section 754; additionally, the NCT-MISSION district caps eating and drinking uses at 179 total, and the records do not show whether a new restaurant would exceed that cap. The address has a complicated history: two prior Conditional Use Authorization applications for restaurants with Type 47 licenses at the adjacent 2575 Mission St were withdrawn (2021, after 3+ years) and cancelled (2018-2021). The site history shows the space was last used as a bar (continuations approved in 1997 and 2005), but no active ABC license is on file. Within 500 feet there are 17 registered food/drink businesses including 3 bars, and 12 active on-sale ABC licenses; within 1,000 feet there are 42 active on-sale licenses, triggering an undue-concentration flag. The block is very active for restaurant applications but few comparable use decisions in the last 5 years provide a meaningful approval rate (N=5: 2 approved with conditions, 3 withdrawn, 0 denied).
data_gaps: The records do not show the current count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION, so it is unknown whether the 179-unit cap has been reached
No hearing transcripts, staff reports, or conditions text are available for the two withdrawn/cancelled CUA applications at 2575 Mission St to explain why they failed
The records do not indicate when the bar use at 2575 Mission St ceased operations or why the space has been vacant since approximately 2017
ABC license conditions are not exposed in the data, so undue-concentration findings or crime statistics for the census tract are not available
No environmental review documents (categorical exemptions, EIR) are extracted for nearby approvals to understand CEQA precedent
The pathway analysis states that merging storefronts is part of the project, but the records do not show whether prior approvals exist for the merger or whether a separate entitlement is needed
